lingq.metaTitle: Readfox vs LingQ: Affordable Open-Source LingQ Alternative
lingq.metaDescription: Compare Readfox and LingQ: {books} free CEFR-graded books, FSRS review, contextual AI lookup, LingQ CSV import, and Plus from {plusPrice}/mo.
lingq.title: Readfox as a LingQ alternative
lingq.summary: Readfox is a calmer, lower-cost alternative to LingQ for learning languages by reading real books. It includes {books} CEFR-graded public-domain books, FSRS spaced repetition, contextual AI lookup, free browser follow-along audio, and direct LingQ CSV word import, with paid plans starting at {plusPrice}/month.

rows.price: Limited free LingQ slots; Premium typically around $12.99/mo billed monthly
rows.freeLibrary: Large community lesson library and mini-stories, mostly gated behind an account
rows.lookup: Community hints and dictionary popups; AI features on higher tiers
rows.review: Built-in flashcards and SRS review tied to LingQ statuses (1–4)
rows.audio: Synced human and TTS audio across many community lessons
rows.offline: Native iOS and Android apps with offline lesson downloads

lingq.migrationHeading: Bring your LingQ vocabulary in under a minute
lingq.migrationBody: Already tracked thousands of words in LingQ? Readfox reads LingQ CSV exports directly and preserves your translations and 1–4 familiarity levels.
lingq.migrationStep1: Export your vocabulary list from LingQ as a CSV file.
lingq.migrationStep2: Open Settings → Known words import in Readfox and upload the CSV.
lingq.migrationStep3: Your known words and familiarity levels apply immediately across every book you open.

readfoxWins.w1: Lower cost: free tier includes {freeLookups} AI word lookups and {freeDetailed} detailed explanations monthly, with Plus from {plusPrice}/mo.
readfoxWins.w2: Cleaner book-reading interface with {books} curated A1–C2 books, FSRS review, and full-library concordance search.
readfoxWins.w3: Open-source AGPL codebase, no ad trackers, and one-step LingQ CSV import.

competitorWins.w1: Supports 40+ languages today, whereas Readfox focuses on a smaller set of polished libraries first.
competitorWins.w2: Includes native mobile apps and a huge catalog of community podcasts and audio mini-stories.
competitorWins.w3: Offers browser extensions for one-click importing from YouTube and streaming sites.

faq.importQ: Can I import my saved words and statuses from LingQ?
faq.importA: Yes. Export your LingQ vocabulary as CSV and upload it in Readfox Settings → Known words import. Readfox maps LingQ statuses directly into your vocabulary list.
faq.freeQ: How much can I use Readfox for free?
faq.freeA: Free accounts get unlimited reading of all {books} free-library books, free on-device dictionary lookups, {freeLookups} AI word lookups, and {freeDetailed} detailed phrase explanations each month.
faq.booksQ: Do I have to upload my own books to start?
faq.booksA: No. Readfox ships {books} public-domain books graded A1 to C2 across English, French, Spanish, Chinese, and Korean, and you can read the first chapter before signing up.
faq.differencesQ: What is the biggest difference between Readfox and LingQ?
faq.differencesA: LingQ offers a broader media ecosystem and 40+ languages at a higher subscription price. Readfox focuses on distraction-free book reading, FSRS review, lower pricing from {plusPrice}/mo, and open-source transparency.

readlang.metaTitle: Readfox vs Readlang: Alternative with Graded Books & FSRS Review
readlang.metaDescription: Compare Readfox and Readlang: {books} built-in A1–C2 books, FSRS review, contextual AI explanations, browser TTS, and plans from {plusPrice}/mo.
readlang.title: Readfox as a Readlang alternative
readlang.summary: Both Readfox and Readlang are indie, reader-first tools for learning languages from real text. Readfox adds {books} built-in CEFR-graded books, server-scheduled FSRS spaced repetition, library concordance search, and browser text-to-speech follow-along, starting free with Plus at {plusPrice}/month.

rows.price: Free tier with daily phrase limits; Premium around $5/mo ($48/yr)
rows.freeLibrary: Community-shared texts and web articles; no curated A1–C2 classic book catalog
rows.lookup: Instant single-word and phrase translation with AI explanations
rows.review: Built-in cloze flashcards with SM-2 style scheduling
rows.audio: TTS playback on flashcards and web texts
rows.import: Strong Chrome/Safari web reader extension, EPUB upload, and web articles
rows.offline: Web app; no offline PWA reader shell

readfoxWins.w1: Ready-to-read catalog of {books} CEFR-graded books with localized titles, blurbs, and zero-signup chapter previews.
readfoxWins.w2: Modern FSRS word review with real example sentences, plus library-wide concordance word search.
readfoxWins.w3: Open-source AGPL software with localized interfaces in 6 languages and free tier from day one (Plus from {plusPrice}/mo).

competitorWins.w1: Readlang's browser Web Reader extension lets you translate any live webpage directly in place.
competitorWins.w2: Supports dozens of languages immediately via web translation backends.
competitorWins.w3: Mature, minimal workflow trusted by independent language learners for over a decade.

faq.freeQ: How does Readfox's free plan compare to Readlang's?
faq.freeA: Readfox includes unlimited reading of all {books} free-library books, free dictionary lookups, {freeLookups} AI lookups, and {freeDetailed} detailed AI answers per month, with paid Plus plans starting at {plusPrice}/mo.
faq.booksQ: Does Readfox require a browser extension?
faq.booksA: No. You can start reading any of the {books} built-in graded books immediately in your browser or phone, or paste a web URL / upload an EPUB into your library.
faq.reviewA: Readfox uses the FSRS spaced-repetition algorithm on the server with multiple review modes and real sentences from books and Tatoeba, plus Anki export.
faq.differencesQ: Should I choose Readfox or Readlang?
faq.differencesA: Pick Readlang if you primarily want a Chrome extension for reading live news websites in dozens of languages. Pick Readfox if you want curated graded books, FSRS review, concordance search, and multilingual UI support.
